title: Pattern generalisers
goal: I can find the rule of a growing pattern and say it in words. I can use the rule for a far figure and backwards.

learn.intro: Look at what stays the same and what grows each time. Make a table. Say the rule in words. Use the rule for any figure, and backwards from a total.

example.problem: Tiles make a plus sign. Figure 1 has 5 tiles and figure 2 has 9 tiles. Figure 3 has arms of 3 tiles. How many tiles are in figure 10? Which figure has 81 tiles?
steps: Each figure has 4 arms and 1 middle tile. In figure n each arm has n tiles.
example.answer: Figure 10 has 41 tiles. Figure 20 has 81 tiles.

howto.title: How to
steps: Count the figures. Make a table.
See what each new figure adds, and why.
Say the rule in words. Use it forwards and backwards.

try.text: Matchstick hexagons are joined in a row. Each new hexagon shares one side with the hexagon before it. How many sticks do 12 hexagons need? {b}
try.explanation: The first hexagon needs 6 sticks. Each new hexagon shares a side, so it adds 5 sticks. Rule: sticks = 5 × hexagons + 1. For 12 hexagons: 5 × 12 + 1 = 61 sticks.

items.text: Matchstick hexagons are joined in a row. Each new hexagon shares one side with the hexagon before it. Figure 1 has 6 sticks. Figure 2 has 11 sticks.
items.explanation: Figure 1 has 6 sticks and figure 2 has 11 sticks (figure 3 has 16). Each new hexagon adds 5 sticks because 1 side is shared. (a) 16 + 5 = 21. (b) 21 + 5 = 26. (c) 5.

items.text: Use the hexagon pattern. Complete the rule and use it.
items.explanation: (a) The first hexagon has 6 sticks, which is 5 + 1. Each new one adds 5. So sticks = 5 × hexagons + 1. (b) 5 × 20 + 1 = 101. (Not 2 × 51: doubling counts the starting stick twice.)

items.text: Mei has some matchsticks. She makes hexagons in a row, as in the pattern.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 100 sticks make at most {b} hexagons, with {b} sticks left over.

items.explanation: (a) 96 - 1 = 95, and 95 ÷ 5 = 19 hexagons. (b) 100 - 1 = 99, and 99 ÷ 5 = 19 with 4 left over. So 19 hexagons use 96 sticks and 4 sticks are left.

items.text: Look at the pattern: 7, 12, 17, 22, ...
items.explanation: Each number is 5 more than the one before. (a) 27 and 32. (b) There are 9 jumps of 5 from the 1st to the 10th: 7 + 9 × 5 = 52. (c) 100 - 7 = 93, and 93 is not a multiple of 5, so 100 is not in the pattern. (Every number ends in 2 or 7.)

items.text: Tiles make a plus sign. Figure n has a middle tile and 4 arms of n tiles each.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The figure with 81 tiles is figure {b}.

items.explanation: Each figure has 4 arms of n tiles and 1 middle tile. (a) 4 × 4 + 1 = 17. (b) 4 × 15 + 1 = 61. (c) The rule is tiles = 4 × figure number + 1. (d) 81 - 1 = 80, and 80 ÷ 4 = 20.

items.text: Adult tickets cost $9 each. Child tickets cost $5 each. A group buys 15 tickets and pays $107 altogether. Make a table to guess and check.
items.explanation: Try 10 adults and 5 children: $90 + $25 = $115, too much. Try 8 adults and 7 children: $72 + $35 = $107. Right. (Another way: all 15 child tickets cost $75. Each adult ticket instead of a child ticket adds $4. $107 - $75 = $32, and 32 ÷ 4 = 8 adult tickets.)

items.text: A shop has 17 stools and chairs. A stool has 3 legs and a chair has 4 legs. There are 61 legs altogether.
items.explanation: Suppose all 17 are stools: 17 × 3 = 51 legs. That is 61 - 51 = 10 legs short. Each chair instead of a stool adds 1 leg, so there are 10 chairs. Then 17 - 10 = 7 stools. Check: 40 + 21 = 61.

items.text: A quiz has 12 questions. A correct answer scores 5 marks. A wrong answer loses 2 marks. Siti answers every question and scores 39 marks.
items.explanation: All 12 right would score 12 × 5 = 60 marks. Each wrong answer costs 5 marks and also loses 2 marks: 7 marks. 60 - 39 = 21, and 21 ÷ 7 = 3 wrong. Then 12 - 3 = 9 right. Check: 45 - 6 = 39.

items.text: Long tables are joined end to end in a row. Each table has 2 chairs on each long side. 1 chair sits at each end.

figure.alt: tables in a row with chairs

items.explanation: 1 table has 6 chairs and 2 tables have 10. Each new table adds 4 chairs (2 on each side). (a) 4 × 5 + 2 = 22. (b) chairs = 4 × tables + 2. (c) 50 - 2 = 48, and 48 ÷ 4 = 12 tables.

items.text: The table shows a pattern.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The figure with 100 sticks is figure {b}.

items.explanation: Each figure adds 3 sticks. Figure 1 has 7 = 3 + 4. (a) sticks = 3 × figure number + 4. (b) 3 × 12 + 4 = 40. (c) 100 - 4 = 96, and 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 10 hexagons need 51 sticks, so 20 hexagons need 102 sticks.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: c
parts.text: No number in the pattern 6, 11, 16, 21, ... ends in 3.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) 101 - 5 = 96 and 96 ÷ 4 = 24, so it is the 25th number: true. (b) 20 hexagons need 5 × 20 + 1 = 101 sticks, not 102: false. (c) The numbers end in 6, 1, 6, 1, ... so none ends in 3: true.

items.text: A purse has 24 coins. Some are 20¢ coins and the rest are 50¢ coins. The coins are worth $9.60 altogether. How many 50¢ coins are there? {b}
items.hint: Suppose all are 20¢ coins. How many cents short is that?
items.explanation: Suppose all 24 coins are 20¢ coins: 24 × 20¢ = $4.80. That is $9.60 - $4.80 = $4.80 short. Each 50¢ coin instead of a 20¢ coin adds 30¢. $4.80 ÷ 30¢ = 16 coins. So 16 fifty-cent coins and 8 twenty-cent coins. Check: $8.00 + $1.60 = $9.60.

items.text: Tiles make staircases. Figure 1 has 1 tile, figure 2 has 3 tiles, figure 3 has 6 tiles and figure 4 has 10 tiles.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The figure with 105 tiles is figure {b}.

items.hint: Figure n adds a column of n tiles. Two staircases make a rectangle.
items.explanation: Figure 10 is 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 10. Two copies of the staircase fit together as a rectangle 10 by 11 = 110 tiles. So one staircase has 55. (b) For figure 14: 14 × 15 = 210 and 210 ÷ 2 = 105. Figure 13 has 91 tiles and figure 15 has 120, so only figure 14 has 105.

items.text: Look at the squares. Each new square adds an L-shaped layer of tiles (shaded). Find 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + ... + 49. The numbers go up by 2 each time. {b}
items.hint: 1, 1 + 3, 1 + 3 + 5: what kind of numbers are they?
items.explanation: 1 = 1 × 1, 1 + 3 = 4 = 2 × 2, 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 = 3 × 3. Each new odd number adds an L-shaped layer to make the next square. The odd numbers up to 49 are 25 numbers (49 = 2 × 25 - 1). So the total is 25 × 25 = 625.

items.text:
Beyond Level 5: Adding a pattern
Add 4 + 7 + 10 + 13 + ... + 100. The numbers go up by 3 each time. {b}
items.hint: How many numbers are there? Pair the first with the last.
items.explanation: From 4 to 100 there are (100 - 4) ÷ 3 = 32 jumps, so 33 numbers. Pair them: 4 + 100 = 104, 7 + 97 = 104, and so on. Each pair makes 104. There are 33 numbers, which is 16 pairs and a middle number 52. 16 × 104 + 52 = 1716. (Or: 33 × 104 ÷ 2 = 1716.)

items.text:
Beyond Level 5: Handshakes
Every person in a group shakes hands once with every other person.
items.hint: n people each shake n - 1 hands. Each handshake counts twice.
items.explanation: (a) Each of the 5 people shakes 4 hands: 5 × 4 = 20. Each handshake is counted twice (once for each person), so 20 ÷ 2 = 10. (b) 12 × 11 = 132, and 132 ÷ 2 = 66 handshakes.

items.text: A quiz has 30 questions. Each right answer scores 4 marks. A wrong answer loses 1 mark. A blank scores 0. Ali leaves 3 questions blank and scores 73 marks. How many questions does he get right? {b}
items.hint: Only answered questions count. Suppose all of them are right.
items.explanation: Ali answers 30 - 3 = 27 questions. All 27 right would score 108 marks. Each wrong answer loses 4 marks and has 1 mark taken away: 5 marks. 108 - 73 = 35, and 35 ÷ 5 = 7 wrong. Right: 27 - 7 = 20. Check: 80 - 7 = 73.

items.text: The numbers go 6, 11, 16, 21, ... What is the 15th number? {b}
items.explanation: Each number is 5 more. There are 14 jumps of 5 from the 1st to the 15th: 6 + 14 × 5 = 76.

items.text: The rule for a pattern is: dots = 3 × figure number + 2. Which figure has 41 dots? {b}
A box holds 20 stools and chairs. A stool has 3 legs and a chair has 4 legs. There are 70 legs altogether. How many chairs are there? {b}
items.explanation: Suppose all 20 are stools: 60 legs. That is 70 - 60 = 10 legs short. Each chair adds 1 leg, so there are 10 chairs (and 10 stools).

items.text: Matchstick hexagons are joined in a row. The rule is sticks = 5 × hexagons + 1. Mei has 130 sticks. What is the most hexagons she can make? {b}
items.explanation: 130 - 1 = 129, and 129 ÷ 5 = 25 with 4 left over. So 25 hexagons use 126 sticks, and 4 sticks are left.
